story.title: Developer obtains reliable independent verification within approved spending
story.intent: Obtain trustworthy independent verification without repeatedly selecting a model that has failed its contract or spending without approval.
story.initialState: A Ticket has actual test evidence. Available model advice, explicit developer routes and observed verification qualification/failure evidence may exist. Paid execution is unapproved by default.
story.action: Request canonical Ticket verification; where paid execution is desired, configure approved providers and tasks and an explicit cumulative spending ceiling for that verification operation.
story.expectedResult: AIWF uses existing Radar advice and llm-utils routing to select an available verification model, with explicit developer routes and spending restrictions taking precedence. It records observed contract qualification/failure separately from advice and avoids automatically selecting a model whose latest observed verification contract failed. The reviewer receives exact valid evidence identifiers and applicable Rule identities. A malformed or incomplete response receives at most one targeted correction containing actual validation errors. Missing mandatory assessments, invalid citations and inconclusive mandatory Rules still block acceptance. Paid execution requires developer approval of provider/task and a spending ceiling; AIWF enforces that ceiling across all scopes/retries of the operation and reports actual usage. Only complete independent acceptance creates a canonical receipt and Done/verified state. No eligible authorized model or exhausted budget yields a truthful blocker, without a receipt. Explicitly configured failed models are not silently overridden; their contract failures remain blocking. Existing Radar, routing, verifier, configuration and Semantika owners only. No new routing engine, duplicate Radar, generic retry or governance subsystem. Preserve historical proof. BASIC Product Intent #2 stays closed; #3 and Consult excluded.
story.exceptions: No eligible authorized model or exhausted budget yields a truthful blocker, without a receipt. Explicitly configured failed models are not silently overridden; their contract failures remain blocking.
story.bounds: Existing Radar, routing, verifier, configuration and Semantika owners only. No new routing engine, duplicate Radar, generic retry or governance subsystem. Preserve historical proof. BASIC Product Intent #2 stays closed; #3 and Consult excluded.
acceptanceCriteria: Verification uses eligible Radar advice, preserves explicit developer routing and spending authority, and records observed qualification separately from advice; failed automatic candidates are avoided.
Exact evidence and Rule identifiers are supplied; at most one targeted correction uses actual validation errors; incomplete, invalid or inconclusive mandatory assessments cannot create acceptance.
Paid providers/tasks and a cumulative per-operation USD ceiling require developer authorization, are enforced across scopes and corrections, and actual usage is reported.

error: Error: Potential conflict with PRODUCT's non-goal of avoiding unnecessary planning ceremonies.

disposition.baseline: 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 assertions. Real public resolve_ticket; three installed mandatory Rules; controlled external inference only. Missing assessments correctly block, but there is one request instead of expected initial plus one targeted correction.
disposition.firstActualDefect: verifyTicketAcceptance passes AcceptanceAssessmentSchema to Asker.json; Rule completeness/citation checks occur after structured validation, outside the existing single correction loop. Missing mandatory assessments therefore do not receive a targeted correction.
disposition.discardedFixtureRuns: Earlier fixture runs omitted mandatory Rules; empty assessment was then legal. Fixture corrected using RuleStore.installDefaults before establishing this baseline. Assertions not weakened.
disposition.requiredDeveloperAnswer: The charter reviewer asks how this Story avoids unnecessary planning ceremonies/artificial hierarchies. Pending proposed answer: existing model selection and verification only; no new user-facing approval ceremony, work hierarchy or governance subsystem.

sourceInvestigation.boundary: ModelRouter already prioritizes explicit configuration and filters usable Radar choices. Asker already has schema-based correction and shared token accounting; reuse these owners. Sibling files had pre-existing changes and were not modified.
